title: Coq au Vin Batch
seoTitle: Coq au Vin Batch | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Red wine-braised chicken with mushrooms and lardons for ten
subtitle: Red wine-braised chicken with mushrooms and lardons for ten
description: Chicken legs and thighs braise in red wine with bacon, mushrooms, pearl onions, and thyme until the sauce is glossy and meat falls from the bone. Serve with boiled potatoes and parsley.

steps.title: Render bacon and brown chicken
steps.instruction: Cook bacon until crisp, set aside. Sear seasoned chicken in bacon fat until golden on all sides, then set aside.

steps.title: Build the braise base
steps.instruction: Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in the same pot 8 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add wine and simmer
steps.instruction: Pour in wine, scrape fond, and reduce 5 minutes. Add broth, thyme, chicken, and bacon. Cover and braise at 325°F or simmer stovetop 60–70 minutes until tender. Target oven/smoker temperature: 325°F.

steps.title: Boil potatoes
steps.instruction: Simmer halved potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, 18–20 minutes. Drain and toss with butter, salt, and parsley.

steps.title: Finish and plate
steps.instruction: Skim excess fat from sauce. Portion chicken and sauce over potatoes, scatter bacon and parsley.

proTips: Beef bouillon cube adds depth if wine flavor feels too sharp.
A beurre manié of butter and flour thickens sauce at the end if needed.
Label wine bottles in the kitchen—braising wine disappears fast in a hall.
tonightSpread: Coq au vin with buttered potatoes and crusty baguette.
Simple green salad with Dijon vinaigrette.
leftovers: Pull meat for wine-braised chicken sandwiches on baguette.
Reduce sauce and serve over pappardelle—different format, same braise.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Coq au vin sounds fancy but it is just smart one-pot cooking—wine, bacon, and time do the work while you prep the rest of the meal. Crews respect a hall that can pull off real French comfort.
mealPrepNotes: Use drinkable wine, not cooking wine. Bacon can be rendered ahead. Braise improves next day if you have leftover capacity.
